A_next_month_ndvi.target_definition: NDVI at month t+1 (HLS monthly mean) where months t and t+1 both have a valid clear-sky granule
A_next_month_ndvi.ranking_rule: score = 0.4*|residual_pearson| + 0.25*|pearson_deseasonalized| + 0.2*|pearson| + 0.15*(mi/max_mi); top 10 shown with at most 2 lags per feature; only (feature, lag) pairs with n >= max(30, min(5% of usable rows, 500)) are rankable; calendar features (doy/month sin-cos) are screened at lag 0 only because they are deterministic and lag-invariant
leakage_flags: Target availability is not random: a region-month enters the panel only if HLS returned a clear-sky granule (valid_coverage>0.1) in BOTH month t and month t+1. The monsoon months are precisely the ones missing, so the panel over-represents dry months and conditions the target on future cloud cover.
ndvi_m at lag 0 is the AR(1) parent of the target: its correlation is persistence, not new information.
Only 139 region-month pairs exist across 7 regions and 58 months (10-34 per region); per-region correlations rest on n=10-34 and are unstable.
Derived from GPM IMERG final-run precipitation; same latency caveat.
Monthly mean of ~10-15 SMAP AM retrievals; sparse, non-random sampling.
ECOSTRESS monthly means rest on few granules with cloud gaps (clear-sky sampling).

B_next_day_soil_moisture.target_definition: SMAP L3 AM soil_moisture_m3_m3 on day t+1; rows kept only where day t+1 is observed

own_series_lag_profile.common_sample_note: no row has all lags [0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 14, 30] observed simultaneously (irregular sampling); lag-to-lag comparisons use different subsets and their n is reported per lag

B_next_day_soil_moisture.ranking_rule: score = 0.4*|residual_pearson| + 0.25*|pearson_deseasonalized| + 0.2*|pearson| + 0.15*(mi/max_mi); top 10 shown with at most 2 lags per feature; only (feature, lag) pairs with n >= max(30, min(5% of usable rows, 500)) are rankable; calendar features (doy/month sin-cos) are screened at lag 0 only because they are deterministic and lag-invariant
leakage_flags: Rows exist only where a SMAP AM retrieval succeeds on day t+1; days with missing retrieval are dropped, so evaluation excludes exactly the conditions (RFI, dense vegetation, frozen ground) where a model would operate blind.

SMAP revisits Bangladesh roughly every 3 days, so the number of usable pairs differs strongly by lag (e.g. lag 1: 874 rows, lag 7: 4,320 rows). The lag profile therefore mixes sampling geometry with physics and must not be read as a decay curve.
smap_am_ffill3d / smap_am at lag 0 are the persistence parent: legitimate at forecast time but not independent information.
soil_moisture_error_m3_m3 is -999 throughout the file (unusable) and was not used.
SMAP AM retrieval exists on only ~38% of days (roughly a 3-day revisit); conditioning on an observed target day selects overpass/quality conditions and is not a random sample.
Last SMAP AM value carried forward up to 3 days - stale by 1-3 days.

C_next_day_rainfall_occurrence.target_definition: 1 if GPM IMERG precipitation on day t+1 >= 1.0 mm/day, else 0
C_next_day_rainfall_occurrence.ranking_rule: score = 0.4*|residual_pearson| + 0.25*|pearson_deseasonalized| + 0.2*|pearson| + 0.15*(mi/max_mi); top 10 shown with at most 2 lags per feature; only (feature, lag) pairs with n >= max(30, min(5% of usable rows, 500)) are rankable; calendar features (doy/month sin-cos) are screened at lag 0 only because they are deterministic and lag-invariant
leakage_flags: GPM IMERG daily totals are accumulated on UTC days: UTC day t covers local 06:00 t to 06:00 t+1, so the day-t predictor window overlaps the first 6 hours of target day t+1.
'final' vs 'late' run: 9,583 of 12,418 region-days are final-run (retrospective only).
Occurrence is binary with a 39% positive rate; Pearson on a binary target is a point-biserial r.
Trailing 7-day rain-day count ending day t; inherits final-run latency.
Trailing 30-day GPM sum ending day t (known at t) but inherits final-run latency.

Amount is highly skewed (48.6% exact zeros, mean 6.2, max 195 mm/day): Pearson is dominated by extremes, Spearman is the more robust summary, and zero-inflation stresses MI estimators (mi_binned is included as an independent check).
'final' vs 'late' run: 9,583 of 12,418 region-days are final-run (retrospective only).

D_monthly_et0_reference.target_definition: Hargreaves ET0 (mm/day, monthly mean) at month t+1
D_monthly_et0_reference.ranking_rule: score = 0.4*|residual_pearson| + 0.25*|pearson_deseasonalized| + 0.2*|pearson| + 0.15*(mi/max_mi); top 10 shown with at most 2 lags per feature; only (feature, lag) pairs with n >= max(30, min(5% of usable rows, 500)) are rankable; calendar features (doy/month sin-cos) are screened at lag 0 only because they are deterministic and lag-invariant
leakage_flags: ET0 is a deterministic function of T2M, T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN, latitude and day-of-year (Hargreaves). Any same-month temperature feature is definitional rather than predictive; with a next-month target the temperature signal is essentially persistence of the seasonal cycle.
et0_m at lag 0 is the same formula applied one month earlier - perfectly collinear with its temperature inputs, so it adds no independent information.
NASA POWER files contain no ET0 variable: this is our own Hargreaves proxy, not an observation, and its skill cannot be validated against a reference ET product here.
The best lags (2-3 months) are a phase artefact of the seasonal cycle: Tmin peaks in the monsoon while ET0 peaks in March-April, so a 2-month offset maximises the sinusoid cross-correlation.

et0.formula: ET0 = 0.0023 * (Tmean + 17.8) * sqrt(Tmax - Tmin) * Ra ; Ra in mm/day (Ra_MJ * 0.408); Ra_MJ = (24*60/pi)*0.0820*dr*(ws*sin(phi)*sin(delta) + cos(phi)*cos(delta)*sin(ws)); dr = 1+0.033cos(2*pi*J/365); delta = 0.409sin(2*pi*J/365 - 1.39); ws = arccos(-tan(phi)tan(delta))
et0.source: computed from NASA POWER T2M, T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN and latitude; the POWER CSVs contain no ET0

notes: ALIGNMENT. Daily panels sit on the exact NASA POWER region-day grid (7 regions x 1,759 days, 2022-01-01..2026-10-25 = 12,313 rows). GPM, SMAP, ECOSTRESS and HLS are left-joined on (date, region) with NO interpolation, so a predictor not measured on that exact day is NaN and is dropped pairwise per (feature, lag); n is reported for every correlation. ECOSTRESS and HLS timestamps were converted UTC -> UTC+6 before assigning a day. Duplicate rows averaged: SMAP AM (28 region-days), ECOSTRESS within local day (all 933 non-null LST retrievals - the qc bit field was not decoded because qc==0 holds for only 1 of them), HLS granules within local day. Monthly panels are calendar-month aggregates of the daily values (means everywhere; SUM for rain_total_m; count of days >= 1 mm for rain_days_m; valid granules only for ndvi_m/ndmi_m/lst_m). GRACE monthly solutions are attached to every day of their month. SRTM elevation and slope are static region constants, cannot vary within a region, and are not used as predictors. TARGETS. Future values within region (shift -1 day / -1 month). A row is usable only where the target itself is observed, so target-sensor sparsity drives n: NDVI 139 region-month pairs, SMAP 4,535 region-days, rainfall 12,306 region-days, ET0 399 region-months. LAG CONVENTION. Lag L means the predictor is measured exactly L days (months) before the last known day/month t and the target is t+1; lag 0 is the most recent observation. Lag columns are built on the FULL grid before filtering, so lag L is exactly L days/months even when a sensor is missing in between. Only lags >= 0 are used, so no target-day predictor enters any correlation. Monthly targets were screened at lags 0-3 (6 and 12 leave too few rows); calendar terms (day-of-year / month sin-cos) were screened at lag 0 only because they are deterministic and lag-invariant. STATISTICS. pearson/spearman are pooled across regions after within-region demeaning, so cross-region mean differences cannot inflate them; per-region values are raw within-region correlations. pearson_deseasonalized additionally removes each region's calendar-month mean (in-sample adjustment: it can remove variance, never add skill). Pooled correlations are systematically higher than per-region ones because the shared monsoon cycle moves all 7 regions together; both are reported. MI. sklearn.mutual_info_regression (n_neighbors=3, random_state=42) on RAW values, with discrete_features flagged for variables having <=20 distinct values. Demeaning a binary target before MI destroys its entropy bound and made the kNN estimator return 2.14 nats against a target entropy of 0.67, so raw values are used; a per-region mean MI is reported alongside (regions with n>=200 daily, n>=40 monthly) as the within-region like-for-like number. mi_binned (plug-in quantile-binned MI, Miller-Madow corrected) is an estimator-independent check and replaces any estimate that exceeds the target entropy. RESIDUAL SIGNAL. Within each region an OLS AR(1) y ~ a + b*y_lag1 is fitted and the predictor is correlated with the AR(1) residual. Descriptive and in-sample, not an out-of-sample gain. A residual r of exactly 0 marks the AR(1) parent feature itself. MODELS. Time split: train <= 2024-12-31 (monthly <= 2024-12), test from 2025-01-01. Baseline is the same AR(1) fitted on train only. Ridge uses RidgeCV (alphas 1e-2..1e3), median imputation and standardisation, with the top 8 features selected on TRAIN ROWS ONLY. y_lag1 (persistence parent) per target: ndvi_m (A), last SMAP AM observation carried forward <= 3 days (B), same-day GPM rainfall/occurrence (C), et0_m (D). Three R2 variants: pooled (as sklearn computes it, includes persistent between-region level differences), within-region (region means removed), anomaly (region x calendar-month means estimated on TRAIN and removed). MAE is in target units (NDVI index, m3/m3, mm/day). RANKING. score = 0.4*|residual_pearson| + 0.25*|pearson_deseasonalized| + 0.2*|pearson| + 0.15*(mi / max mi), at most 2 lags per feature shown. Only (feature, lag) pairs observed on n >= max(30, min(5% of usable rows, 500)) rows are rankable; weaker-coverage sensors (HLS NDVI/NDMI, ECOSTRESS LST) are listed separately in below_threshold_sensor_signals. SCOPE. Screening is descriptive and has no multiplicity control: ~20-30 features x 4-7 lags are tested per target, at n as low as 139, so individual correlations with |r| < 0.2 at the monthly sample size should not be trusted.
